clue.text: Wild creature who retains skill with golf

indicators.note: retains means the word who holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: taken as written
art is skill, as in the art of persuasion
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A wild animal that keeps up its skills on the golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: The warthog is a wild African pig, so it is an example of a wild creature.

clue.text: Accompanying card — hearts

parts.note: a card is a witty, amusing person, so a wit
H is the abbreviation for hearts in card games

explanation.surface: A card played alongside a heart in a hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Card' looks like a playing card beside 'hearts', but it is the old sense of a funny person.
explanation.definitionFit: The preposition means together with or alongside, the sense of accompanying someone.

clue.text: Call to make of use of foil, say, in reserve

parts.note: to ring someone is to call them on the phone

parts.words: make of use of foil, say
parts.note: a foil is a sword used in fencing, so using one is to fence

explanation.surface: An instruction to phone and arrange to use some kitchen foil kept in reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: To ring-fence money is to set it aside for one purpose only, guaranteeing it as a reserve.

clue.text: Lower chamber here to prove if US Senate's corrupt

indicators.note: corrupt means the letters of the preceding words are spoilt into a new order

parts.words: here to prove if US Senate's
parts.note: the possessive here is read as 'Senate is', so its S counts

explanation.surface: A claim that the lower chamber exists to prove that the US Senate is corrupt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corrupt' rearranges all the letters of 'here to prove if US Senate's', including the S of the apostrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: In the US Congress the House of Representatives is the lower legislative chamber, below the Senate.

clue.text: Is game controlled by eg backward look?

indicators.note: controlled by means the next pieces are held inside the turned letters
backward means the letters of eg are read from right to left

parts.note: taken as written
a game leg is a lame one, so game means limp
is can be shortened to 's, giving a lone S

explanation.surface: A question whether some game is run by a quick look back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backward' turns EG to GE, and 'controlled by' puts LIMPS (game is: limp's) inside it. 'Game' here means lame, as in a game leg.
explanation.definitionFit: A glimpse is a brief look at something, a fleeting sight.

clue.text: Bitter jam almost like whole fruit?

indicators.note: almost means the word jam loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written
fruit left whole has not been chopped into cubes, so it is undiced

explanation.surface: A jam made almost entirely of whole, unchopped fruit, tasting bitter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bitter' looks like a flavour of the jam, but it is the definition, in the sense of resentful.
explanation.definitionFit: A jaundiced view is a bitter, resentful or cynical one.

clue.text: Raise audible sound of paper dog

parts.note: to jack up a car is to raise it

indicators.note: audible means the following word is said aloud and spelt another way

parts.note: the crackling noise paper makes is a rustle

explanation.surface: A dog that perks up at the rustling of a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: The Jack Russell is a breed of small terrier, so an example of a dog.

clue.text: Last chance to have easy debut when playing

indicators.note: playing means the letters of the two words frolic into a new order

explanation.surface: A sporting newcomer's last chance to make an easy first appearance.
explanation.definitionFit: The use-by date on food is the final day it should be eaten, the last chance to have it.

clue.text: Look, look! Kedgeree on the counter for a stretch

indicators.note: on the counter says the hidden letters are read backwards
for a stretch says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone telling a friend to look at the kedgeree that has sat on the kitchen counter for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the counter' reads like a kitchen worktop but means going against the usual direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Dekko is British slang for a quick look, as in 'have a dekko'.

clue.text: Joint leader to arrest citizen

parts.note: to cop someone is slang for catching or arresting them
a citizen of a place is one of its residents

explanation.surface: A joint leader ordering the arrest of a citizen.
explanation.definitionFit: A co-president shares the top office with another, so leads jointly.

clue.text: Swerve heartless rat

indicators.note: heartless means the central letter of the synonym is taken out

parts.note: to deflect is to swerve or turn aside

explanation.surface: A cruel rat that swerves out of the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rat' looks like the animal but is a verb: to desert one's side.
explanation.definitionFit: To rat on a group is to abandon it for the other side, which is to defect.

clue.text: Uncovered spicy Indian food

indicators.note: uncovered means the synonym has its outer letters stripped away

parts.note: spicy can mean racy or sexy, so erotic

explanation.surface: Exposed hot Indian dishes, or a stripping that is a little risque.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spicy' suggests curry, fitting the surface, but it means racy here.
explanation.definitionFit: Roti is an Indian unleavened flatbread, a staple of Indian cooking.

clue.text: Huge cocaine bust

indicators.note: bust means broken, so the letters of cocaine are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A newspaper headline about an enormous drugs raid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bust' reads as a police raid but signals that the letters are broken up.
explanation.definitionFit: Oceanic means vast as an ocean, so huge or immense.

clue.text: Policy example in which city no longer replaces Tesla

indicators.note: replaces means one piece swaps in for another inside the synonym

parts.note: an instance is an example of something
T is the symbol for the tesla, the unit of magnetic flux density
Ur was an ancient Mesopotamian city that no longer exists

explanation.surface: A sample policy in which a car brand is swapped for another city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tesla' suggests the car maker, but it is the physics unit, symbol T.
explanation.definitionFit: An insurance policy is a contract of cover, and the word alone can stand for one.

clue.text: Slipping down unnoticed?

parts.note: down is a bird's soft feathers, which shed rain without anyone noticing

explanation.surface: Something sliding down without anyone seeing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down' means feathers: water slides off a bird's plumage without effect, as criticism slides off someone unaffected.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes criticism that has no effect on someone, slipping off harmlessly.

clue.text: Possibly French creep — I'm scared, ironically

parts.note: French is an example of a language, or tongue
to inch along is to creep slowly
eek is a cry of fright

explanation.surface: Someone joking that a French lover creeping up frightens them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French' hints at a kiss but is just one example of a language.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something tongue-in-cheek means saying it with mock seriousness, ironically.

clue.text: Bloated nature of beasts regularly stalking seabird

indicators.note: stalking means following behind, so these letters come after the bird

parts.note: the puffin is a seabird of the North Atlantic

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of beasts is taken

explanation.surface: A wildlife scene of bloated animals following a seabird.
explanation.definitionFit: Puffiness is the state of being swollen, so bloated nature.

clue.text: A pretty far out get-together later

indicators.note: out means the letters of the phrase are put out of order

explanation.surface: A party held a long way from home.
explanation.definitionFit: An afterparty is a gathering held after a main event, so a later social gathering.

clue.text: Daily might have this relevance, on going abroad

indicators.note: abroad can mean astray or widely scattered, so the letters wander into a new order

explanation.surface: A newspaper's relevance changing when it goes overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'daily' is a British term for a cleaner who comes in every day, not a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A daily, a domestic cleaner, might well carry a product for scouring ovens.

clue.text: Veto very loud Rocky location

parts.note: to veto is to ban
FF, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud

explanation.surface: A rule forbidding loud noise at a rocky site.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rocky' is the Rocky Mountains: Banff is a resort town in the Canadian Rockies.
explanation.definitionFit: Banff sits in the Rocky Mountains of Alberta, so it is a location in the Rockies.

clue.text: Splits in wings of Bahai religious groups

indicators.note: the wings of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: sects are religious groups that break away

explanation.surface: Factions splitting off from the Bahai faith into sects.
explanation.definitionFit: To bisect is to cut into two parts, so it splits.

clue.text: Area of England where each second taste reflected trouble

parts.note: a tang is a sharp taste

indicators.note: reflected means the word for trouble is read backwards, as in a mirror

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: A region of England where every taste test was reflected in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: EAST ANGLIA is the eastern bulge of England, covering Norfolk and Suffolk.
explanation.definitionFit: East Anglia is a region in the east of England, so an area of the country.

clue.text: Perhaps Mercedes spots Georgia is angry

parts.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia
someone who rages is very angry

explanation.surface: Mercedes, perhaps a woman, notices that Georgia is in a fury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mercedes' looks like a person's name and 'spots' like a verb, but the cars are kept in the spots.
explanation.definitionFit: Garages are places where cars such as Mercedes are kept, so their parking spots.

clue.text: Preserve recurrent dance

indicators.note: recurrent means the word comes back again, so it appears twice

parts.note: to can food is to preserve it in tins

explanation.surface: Keeping a dance going over and over.
explanation.definitionFit: The cancan is a high-kicking Parisian music-hall dance.

clue.text: My fault, carrying about islander

parts.note: cor is an exclamation of surprise, like 'my!'

indicators.note: carrying means the word for fault holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: a sin is a fault or wrongdoing
ca, circa, is Latin for about

explanation.surface: Someone owning up to a mistake while carrying something round.
explanation.definitionFit: A Corsican is a native of Corsica, a Mediterranean island, so an islander.

clue.text: Ship worker from east travelled on old fighters to the west

indicators.note: in an across clue, going west means reading the pieces right to left

parts.note: rode means travelled on a horse or vehicle
vets are veterans, old soldiers

explanation.surface: A dock worker from the east who rode in with old soldiers heading west.
explanation.definitionFit: A stevedore loads and unloads ships at a dock, so is a ship worker.

clue.text: Wealth of old US VP keeping useful when body's gone

indicators.note: keeping means the vice-president's name holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: Mike Pence was US vice-president under Trump

indicators.note: the body of a word is its middle, so only its outer letters remain

explanation.surface: The riches of a former US vice-president kept useful after he is dead.
explanation.definitionFit: Opulence is great wealth and luxurious abundance.

clue.text: Weird anger coming back in middle of week

indicators.note: in means the turned letters sit inside the middle pair

coming back means the word for anger is read backwards

parts.note: ire is anger

explanation.walkthrough: 'coming back' turns IRE to ERI, which goes 'in' EE, the middle of 'week'.
explanation.definitionFit: Eerie means strange and unsettling, so weird.

clue.text: Starting late, 12 is too old

indicators.note: starting late means the word loses its first letter, as if it began a step later

explanation.walkthrough: '12' is not a number but the answer to 12-down, a policy, whose synonym loses its first letter.

clue.text: Compound in Kentucky surrounded by everyone

indicators.note: surrounded by means the state abbreviation is held inside the word for everyone

parts.note: all means everyone
KY is the postal abbreviation for Kentucky

explanation.surface: A compound in Kentucky with people all around it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Compound' suggests a fenced enclosure, but it is the chemical sense.

clue.text: Doctor curing belly by nasty treatment from afar?

clue.text: Nipper beginning to tuck into German drink

indicators.note: into means the initial letter goes inside the German word

parts.note: Bier is German for beer

indicators.note: beginning to means only the first letter of tuck is used

explanation.walkthrough: 'Nipper' looks like a British word for a small child, but it means something that nips.

clue.text: Spoil tie with lump after leaving B&B

indicators.note: after leaving means the named letters depart from the two synonyms

parts.note: to bind is to tie

B and B, the letters of bed and breakfast

explanation.walkthrough: 'after leaving B&B' removes one B from each synonym.

clue.text: They've initially worn outside footwear covered in grass

clue.text: Grass cutting with colour unaffected

clue.text: Lush, very large mountain, as it were

explanation.surface: A description of a lush, very large mountain landscape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lush' looks like an adjective for green slopes but is a noun meaning a drinker.

clue.text: Broadcast naked stills?

clue.text: Ugly cad messed around with rifles in a shocking way

clue.text: Hoax, inflammatory online activity only seen after each opening?

clue.text: Foolish way to work, using sarcasm to throw leader

clue.text: Most of eg October and November carving incomplete black and white landmark

clue.text: Allure before and after lady's first dance

clue.text: Standard opera line

explanation.definitionFit: Normal means usual or conforming to a standard.

clue.text: What's left in fireside bar if tipped over you
